svg.title: A worker crash and a replay from the event history
svg.desc: The charge activity has a recorded result. After the worker exits, a new worker replays the workflow, receives that recorded result, and starts the ship activity.
svg.text: Workflow code, replayed
1. Charge the card.
Activity. Side effect at the bank.
2. Ask the warehouse to ship.
Activity. Runs after charge has a result.
3. Wait 14 days, then send a note.
Timer stored by the service.
The worker process can exit during the wait.
A worker picks the workflow up when it fires.
Event history, kept by the service
Workflow started. Order 4812.
Charge completed.
Result: payment id, stored here.
Ship: still open.
The result line is absent so far.
This log lives outside the worker.
A deploy can replace the worker process.
What the new worker does
The first worker exits after the charge result is in the history and before ship runs.
A new worker loads the history and runs the same workflow code from the top.
Charge returns the recorded payment id. The bank is left alone on this replay.
Ship starts, because the history has an opening there.
If the charge succeeded at the bank and the result was lost before it was recorded,
the activity runs again. The order id, sent as an idempotency key, makes the bank
return the original payment. The history then records that result once.
